intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). This badge takes you on an exciting journey to understand how psychology impacts everyday life and leadership. You’ll learn about famous psychologists and their contributions, create and perform a skit showing psychology in action, explore mental health and resilience, and track your own activities and emotions to see how they shape your well-being. Along the way, you’ll practice empathy, reflect on the Scout Oath and Law, and even design your own pledge to inspire hope and support in your community. Finally, dive into career paths in psychology and discover what it takes to succeed in this fascinating field. Expand your mind, build resilience, and make a difference—start your Psychology Badge adventure today!

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While preparing for a high-adventure trek, a patrol leader notices a Scout becoming overwhelmed when trying to memorize 15 wilderness safety rules all at once. Using cognitive psychology principles of working memory, what teaching strategy works best?
options: Read all 15 rules faster without pausing so they enter long-term memory immediately.
Use chunking and spaced practice: group the 15 rules into 3 meaningful categories (such as S.T.O.P. or ABCDE) and practice retrieving them across multiple hands-on scenarios.
Skip practice and rely only on passive re-reading right before the trek.
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B — Apply chunking and active spaced retrieval to organize information within human working-memory limits (4 to 7 items) and consolidate long-term recall.
quiz_item.explanation: Human working memory holds only a few chunks at once; grouping items into meaningful frameworks and practicing active recall builds durable neural pathways.

Core Standard 1 (Req 5): (a) In your own words, define empathy and give examples of how you might show empathy to others.
Core Standard 2 (Req 5): (b) Discuss the importance of resilience and how Scouting experiences develop resilience.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Review Standard (Req 5): Read the official Psychology requirement and identify the key questions, terms, or skills covered in Practicing Empathy & Developing Resilience in Scouting.
Step 2 - Gather Evidence & Examples: Research the required facts in the Psychology Test Lab Guide and record structured notes in your Scout Workbook.

Step 3 - Practice & Apply (Demonstrate): Work with your patrol buddy or family (as required) to demonstrate each element of Practicing Empathy & Developing Resilience in Scouting with concrete real-world examples.
Step 4 - Counselor Conference & Sign-Off: Present your completed workbook organizer and demonstrate your understanding to your Merit Badge Counselor for Blue Card verification.
